To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we produced a family of monoclonal antibodies that inhibit the signalling induced by IL-1 and other cytokines that share a common receptor chain, gp130.
we have produced a series of mAb against the gp130 chain of the IL- 6 receptor.

we have developed a family of monoclonal antibodies directed against the gp130 chain of the IL- 6 receptor, which are able to inhibit the signalling induced by various cytokines of the same receptor family.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of new epitopes on the gp130 chain, the study of their structure and function, the development of new reagents for the detection of the gp130 cytokines and the development of specific neutralizing mAb.
the study of the structure-function relationships of gp130, a signal transducer chain of the cytokine family involved in inflammatory and tumoral diseases.
the identification of gp130 epitopes involved in the signaling of the IL-1 family of cytokines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
gp130 contains several distinct domains involved in the binding of the cytokine-receptor complexes.
the gp130 molecule is involved in the signaling of several cytokines of the IL- 6 family, and that this signaling is mediated through different epitopes of the gp130 molecule.
gp130 has a complex structure with several domains that can be specifically targeted to neutralize the activity of different cytokines of the IL- 6 family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the gp130 chain of the IL- 6 receptor is composed of 4 domains, each of them being able to interact with the ligand-receptor complex and with one of the cytokines of this family.
we have identified 3 epitopes involved in the IL-6 signaling, one of them being the binding site of the IL-61-6R complex on gp130.

the gp130 receptor has at least 2 different domains involved in IL- 6 signaling: one is involved in the interaction with the IL6-IL- 6R complex and another is involved in the activation of the signal transduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
gp130 can be divided into 3 distinct domains, each of which is involved in the binding of one cytokine of the gp130 cytokine family.
we have identified a new epitope of the IL-1R1 chain which is not involved in the binding of IL-1 to IL-1R but which is essential for signal transduction.
we identified several new gp130 epitopes involved in the signalling of IL-6, OM, LIF and CNTF.
